set.n: James Webster's forgotten buried money, Clay Township near Eldora
set.pl: GNIS Eldora; "four miles from Eldora", direction not given
set.st: In May 1897 the Steamboat Rock Echo reported that James Webster of Clay Township, who distrusted banks, had buried about $1,000 of pension money and several hundred dollars more, then forgot the spot; searching failed. Wire copies that spring inflated it to $50,000 in casks on a tenant farm four miles from Eldora. No later find was reported.
set.t: The local amount (about $1,000-1,500) is the believable one. Place Webster in Clay Township on an 1890s Hardin plat. Access: private: permission.
src: Steamboat Rock Echo 20 May 1897 p3 'Buried his Money' (Newspapers.com 14772299, PC read
wire copies May-Sept 1897 (Rock Island Argus 3 Jun 1897, Paducah Daily Sun 3 Jun 1897, LoC)

set.n: Reuben Bennett, the Hamilton County miser, farm 2 mi from Webster City
set.y: lived there c.1878-1898; died autumn 1898; searched to 1903
set.pl: Papers: 800-acre farm 'two miles from the city' (Webster City), next to the county poor farm; direction not given, pin at Webster City with a 3.5 km ring
set.st: Reuben Bennett, formerly of Portsmouth, Ohio, lived alone for about twenty years in a small hut on his 800-acre farm two miles from Webster City, refusing to sell hay or stock; the manager of the neighbouring poor farm found him dead in bed in autumn 1898. Relatives and a daughter from Helena fought over the estate, and in 1903 relatives were still searching for his buried thousands, which had not been found.
set.t: Only one 1903 paragraph says relatives were searching for buried money; the 1898 accounts (Cresco, Humboldt Republican 1 Dec 1898) describe the miser and his $30,000 estate (won by his daughter in 1902) but no hidden money. Place the 800 acres on a Hamilton plat. Access: private.
src: Kansas City Journal 27 Nov 1898 p18 (Helena corr., Chicago Daily News)
Manchester Democrat 3 Jun 1903 p3 (LoC Chronicling America)
Ottumwa Courier 29 Nov 1902 p1 (Newspapers.com, PC read)

set.n: North Henderson bank loot in a farm barn, 4 mi W of North Henderson (found)
set.pl: Henderson Co. Graphic-Reporter 22 May 1913: a farm 'four miles west of North Henderson'; pin 4 mi W of GNIS North Henderson
set.st: After the May 1913 North Henderson bank robbery, $639.75 in silver was found in satchels hidden under a pile of corn fodder in a barn on a farm four miles west of North Henderson, and $92.80 on the two captured men. About $530 of the roughly $1,260 taken was never accounted for, but nothing ties it to a spot.
set.t: FOUND: the barn cache was emptied in 1913; the missing $530 has no known hiding place. Access: private.
src: Henderson Co. Graphic-Reporter 22 May 1913 p1 (Newspapers.com 1013307136, PC read)

set.n: Henry Onnen's henhouse jars and missing coin collection, Minonk
set.pl: Woodford County Journal 8 Oct 1942: Onnen was a Minonk recluse (not Eureka, where the suit was heard); GNIS Minonk, home not placed
set.st: Henry W. Onnen, 65, a Minonk recluse who distrusted banks and courts, died in October 1941. His will told three nephews to dig under the henhouse 'all at once'; they found about $7,000 in fruit jars ($6,400 in bills and seven jars of silver) and an old trunk with $3,000 more. In 1942 his sister sued, saying an old coin collection once appraised at $20,000 was missing.
set.t: The henhouse cache was dug; the coin collection was never found. Place Onnen's home near Minonk on a 1940s Woodford plat. Access: private.
src: Woodford County Journal 8 Oct 1942 p1 'Buried Treasure Suit' (Newspapers.com 1041676264, PC read)

set.n: James Hudson's $1,200 he hid twice, farm at Dover
set.st: James Hudson came back from the West, bought a small farm at Dover and buried $1,200 in an earthen jar; fox hunters' dogs dug it up and brought it to him, and he hid it again so well his failing memory lost it.
set.t: Probably newspaper filler: the only other copy found is a bank advertisement ('Moral: Deposit your money...'), and the Bureau County Tribune has nothing. Likely invented. Access: private.
src: Republican and Herald 22 Nov 1913 p3 and other copies (TN TreasureNet Treasure Legends thread 700240, 708682)

set.n: Murdered man's money at the old sugar camp near Patterson
set.pl: GNIS Patterson (village); sugar camp "near here", not located
set.st: July 1907: two Patterson men dug up a considerable sum (guessed at $5,000, probably less) near the site of an old sugar camp. The money was believed hidden by a murdered man; local legends surround the spot and more was believed hidden there. Others joined the search.
set.t: One wire 'special' only (Des Moines Register 25 Jul 1907 p2): found near an old sugar camp with a spirit medium's help; amount untold; no distance. No local account. Access: private: permission.
src: Evening Times-Republican (Marshalltown) 25 Jul 1907 (TN TreasureNet Treasure Legends thread 562278, 616175)

set.n: Herman Lunning's hidden money, recluse's farm near Dubuque
set.st: Jan 1916: aged recluse Herman Lunning was found dying at his farm near Dubuque, struck down by robbers; he was known to have large sums of money, presumably hidden on his farm.
set.t: Wire only; no 1916 Dubuque paper online. Rumoured money 'hidden away on his farm'; no later find. Place Lunning's farm near Dubuque on a 1910s plat. Access: private.
src: El Paso Herald 24 Jan 1916 (TN TreasureNet Treasure Legends thread 615030)
